This is a Node.js API with five pieces that stack neatly.

**The stack, bottom to top:**

`store.js` holds the data — an in-memory map of users and orders. Each record lives for 15 minutes after it's written, then expires.

`cache.js` sits in front of the store. It's a 256-slot LRU cache that remembers reads so repeated queries don't hit the store. No time limit — it only clears out old entries when you hit the size cap.

`routes.js` defines the three endpoints: `GET /users` and `GET /orders` read from the cache, `POST /orders` writes straight to the store and bypasses the cache.

`auth.js` validates bearer tokens using HMAC-SHA256. Tokens are signed with a shared secret from the environment. Every token is a userId plus its signature.

`server.js` is the front door. It creates an HTTP server that checks the auth header on every request, rejects anything unsigned, then hands the authed request to the router.

When a request comes in, it flows: check token → route lookup → read from cache (or store if it's a miss) → write returns straight to store.
